brief: Two pairs of bases. Bolt the two bases of each pair together, with no connector inside a pair. Put the pairs side by side and fit a side connector on every wall where one pair touches the other.

requirements.evidence: Four full bases at 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0 / 1,1 on level 0 form a 2x2 block. Pairs run along r: pair A = piece:0,0,0;full + piece:0,1,0;full, pair B = piece:1,0,0;full + piece:1,1,0;full. check_build reports groups [[0,0, 0,1], [1,0, 1,1]].

jointBolt:0#0,1#0 bolts pair A's wall 0,0|0,1 and jointBolt:0#1,1#2 bolts pair B's wall 1,0|1,1. One bolt fills the wall (further bolts on that wall return ALREADY_FITTED). Joint bolts, not connectors, are what check_build counts as bolting a wall into one body.
requirements.requirement: Bolt the two bases of each pair together

requirements.evidence: No connector sits on 0,0|0,1 or 1,0|1,1; connectors fitted live only on the three cross-pair walls. The two connectors briefly placed on within-pair walls were removed, and the bolt briefly placed on cross wall 0,0|1,0 was removed.

The two groups touch on three walls of the 2x2 block: 0,0|1,0, 0,1|1,1 and the diagonal 0,1|1,0, and connector:0#0,0|1,0, connector:0#0,1|1,1, connector:0#0,1|1,0 are fitted on all three; find_sockets for connectors returns no further offers. The diagonal wall is where the two pairs touch diagonally in this block, so leaving it bare would have under-joined the pairs; it is included and flagged here so the choice is visible.
requirements.requirement: Pairs side by side with a side connector on every wall where one pair touches the other

requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces fitted 14 solid end caps on the outside faces. lockJoints was deliberately not run: it auto-bolts every touching wall, including the three cross-pair walls, which would put bolts where the brief wants connectors. check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no issues.
requirements.requirement: House rules: cap open faces and lock joints

finish.summary: A 2x2 block of four full bases at level 0, arranged as two pairs running along r: pair A = (0,0)+(0,1), pair B = (1,0)+(1,1). Each pair is held together by a joint bolt on its shared wall and has no connector on that wall. The two pairs are joined by side connectors on all three walls where they touch: the two straight walls (0,0|1,0 and 0,1|1,1) plus the diagonal wall 0,1|1,0 that a 2x2 hex block creates between the pairs. check_build passes with meshClash clear and two groups, one per pair. Open outside faces are capped; lockJoints was not run because it would bolt the cross-pair walls that the brief reserves for connectors.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

lines.key: pvc-section-double  (cut 18 mm from 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US))
lines.label: pvc-section-double (cut 18 mm from 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US))

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes

events.text: Four bases in two bolted pairs, side connectors only between pairs — I'll map the layout, then bolt and connect exactly where the brief specifies.

result.note: These ops were refused ALREADY_FITTED or NO_CHANGE (that state already holds), so the batch was applied again without them.

events.text: Unexpected — pair A's second bolt was dropped as "already fitted", suggesting one bolt fills a whole wall. Let me get the true state before adding anything more.
Now both pairs are bolted and the remaining bolt offers are only the cross-pair sides. Next, the side connectors on the cross-pair walls.

result.note: A side connector joins two bases that stand side by side on the same storey. Bases that touch with no connector on the wall between them are one body (joint bolts); every wall between two groups needs a connector, walls inside a group stay bare. get_build lists each touching wall and the groups. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: All connectors are fitted and none are left to offer. Now verifying the topology, capping open faces, and running the final check.
